title: The scarecrow went for a walk
teaser: Dolores's porch scarecrow turned up on the Gay Street bridge, facing the river. Work out who was there.
scene: Dolores has had a scarecrow on her porch since the first of October. Flannel shirt, straw hat, a face she painted herself and will not let anyone call creepy.
This morning the porch was empty.

The scarecrow turned up a little later on the Gay Street bridge, propped against the railing and facing the river, like it had paid for the view. Nothing was damaged. The hat was on straight. Somebody had even tucked the flannel in.

Dolores is not upset, exactly. She would just like to know. Frank, next door, says he heard nothing, which Dolores says is what Frank always hears. Gus says Biscuit, his beagle, was home all night, which nobody asked.
Five neighbors were out early, each at a different spot, at a different hour, carrying a different thing. One of them was at the Gay Street bridge.
question: Who was at the Gay Street bridge?

clues.text: Gus: "Frank was out earlier than Imani. Don't ask me how I know. Small town."
Frank: "Whoever was at Lock 60 was out at ten. You can look that up."
Dolores: "Gus was out earlier than Walt. Somebody on this block has to keep track, and it isn't Frank."
Walt, tapping two lines in his notebook: "Whoever was out at seven had a thermos."
"Here's what I know for sure," Ruthie says. "Whoever was at Reeves Park was out at nine."
Imani: "Whoever was out at eleven had a tote bag. It's in my field notes."
Ruthie, lowering her voice: "Whoever was at Lock 60 had a camera. I'm not naming names."
Dolores: "Walt was out at seven, or at eight, hon. One or the other."
Frank: "Ruthie was at the Schuylkill River Trail or at the French Creek Trail. I'm not going to pretend I know which."
Gus shrugs: "Frank had a pie dish or had a camera."
Walt, checking his notebook: "Whoever was at the Schuylkill River Trail had a thermos."

reveal: Walt. He was on the Gay Street bridge at eight with a folding chair under one arm and the scarecrow under the other. He propped it against the railing, tucked in the flannel and sat with it a while. His reasoning: it had spent five weeks on a porch looking at a hedge, and it deserved to see the river once before the season ended.
Dolores has decided this is sweet. Frank has decided it is theft. They are both still talking about it, which is the most they have agreed on since 1996.

title: The heron count went missing
teaser: The morning's bird count vanished off a bench at Black Rock Sanctuary. Work out who was there.
scene: Saturday is count day at Black Rock Sanctuary. A few birders walk the wetland paths at first light, write down every heron, duck and kingfisher, and leave the tally on a clipboard on a bench so the next shift can add to it.
Last Saturday the next shift found the bench. No clipboard.

Nobody thinks it was stolen, exactly. Nobody steals a bird count. But it is gone, and the birding club's president has already used the word "unacceptable" twice. Ruthie is offering a free coffee to anyone with information, which has produced a great deal of information.
Biscuit, Gus's beagle, has been mentioned. Biscuit is always mentioned.
Five regulars were out early, each at a different spot, at a different hour, carrying a different thing. One of them was at Black Rock.
question: Who was at Black Rock Sanctuary?

categories.question: When was each of them out?

clues.text: Gus: "Biscuit was out at eleven, or at ten. One of those. I was elbow deep in a derailleur."
Ruthie: "Imani had a folding chair, or had a tote bag. My sources split down the middle."
Frank: "Whoever was at the Schuylkill River Trail had a camera. You can look that up."
Imani, flipping a page: "Walt was out at ten, or at eight. My notes stop being useful right there."
Dolores: "Ruthie was at Lock 60, or at the Schuylkill River Trail. I had my reading glasses on, not my walking ones."
Walt, checking his notebook: "Whoever was out at nine had a thermos."
Frank, grudgingly: "Whoever was out at seven had a bike pump. Dolores and I agree on that, so mark the calendar."
Ruthie, lowering her voice: "Whoever was at the Gay Street bridge was out at ten. I'm not naming names."
Walt, tapping two lines in his notebook: "Whoever was at Reeves Park was out at seven."
Gus shrugs: "Imani was out at eight or at seven."
Dolores: "Imani had a bike pump, or had a folding chair, hon. One or the other."

reveal: Imani. She was at Black Rock at eight with a folding chair and a strong opinion. The clipboard said eleven great blue herons. Imani had counted four, so she took the clipboard home to check it against her own notes before anyone could send it in. It was four. She would like that noted.
Biscuit, for the record, was on the Schuylkill River Trail at eleven with a camera, and nobody has explained that either.

title: The soup walked off
teaser: A thermos of homemade soup walked off the fence at Lock 60. Work out who was there.
scene: Lock 60 sits across the river in Mont Clare, the only working lock left on the Schuylkill Canal, and on a cold Saturday it is a fine place to drink soup out of a thermos.

That was the plan, anyway. A woman from the next street over set her green thermos on the fence by the lock (minestrone, homemade, still hot) and walked the towpath for twenty minutes. When she came back, the fence was bare.
She is not angry. She is hungry. She has started describing the soup to anyone who will stand still. Walt has offered to check his notebook. Ruthie has offered a coffee to whoever finds it.
Five people were out that morning, each at a different spot, at a different hour, carrying a different thing. One of them was at Lock 60.
question: Who was at Lock 60?

Ruthie, wiping down the coffee cart: "Frank had a tote bag or had a bike pump. Two stories going around, and one of them's right."
Frank, grudgingly: "Whoever was out at nine had a bike pump. Dolores and I agree on that, so mark the calendar."
Walt, checking his notebook: "Whoever was out at seven had a tote bag."
Dolores: "Imani was out at seven, or at eight, hon. One or the other."

reveal: Ruthie. She was at Lock 60 at ten with a pie dish in one hand, saw a green thermos on the fence and picked it up, because she owns four green thermoses and they all look like that. She found out at lunch, one sip in.
The rest of the minestrone has gone home with a coffee on the house, and Ruthie has asked that the matter be considered closed.

title: The potluck pie is gone
teaser: The potluck pie left Reeves Park before the potluck got there. Work out who was there.
scene: Every year on the Saturday before Thanksgiving, the block carries a dish each to a picnic table in Reeves Park and calls it a potluck. Nobody organizes it. It just happens.

This year somebody brought the pie early. A whole pumpkin pie, from scratch, left on the table under a dish towel to hold the spot. When the rest of the block arrived with their casseroles and their bags of rolls, the towel was still there. The pie was not.
There are theories. Most of them involve Biscuit, Gus's beagle, who has a record. Gus says Biscuit was with him all morning, then says most of the morning, then stops talking.
Five regulars were out that morning, each at a different spot, at a different hour, carrying a different thing. One of them was at Reeves Park.
